cards.explanation: The answer is False. The landowner rented the vineyard out to the tenants and "…went away on a journey." He didn't hang around the vineyard watching them work. Renting it out and leaving is how the parable starts, friends.

The answer is to collect his share of the fruit. Verse 34 says that when harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to collect his share of the fruit. It's his vineyard, so the fruit has an owner. The servants are there for the share and nothing else, friends.

The answer is that he sends more servants than the first group. Verse 36 says he sent other servants, more than the first group. Then the tenants did the same to them. Sending a bigger group after what just happened? I'd have sent a strongly worded letter, and that's about it.
The answer is son. Verse 37 says, "Finally, he sent his son to them." After the servants, the landowner sends his son. I think that tells you something about where this story is headed, friends.

The answer is True. When the landowner sends his son, he says, "They will respect my son…" (Matthew 21:37). That's the landowner's own hope as the son goes, and the words come straight from him. Hold onto that line, friends, because the very next verse is where it gets rough.

The answer is his inheritance. The tenants say, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’ They see the heir and go straight to the inheritance. I think this is a heavy part of the parable, friends.

The answer is that they say he will bring the tenants to a wretched end and rent the vineyard to others. Verse 41 has them saying, "He will bring those wretches to a wretched end…" and that he "…will rent out the vineyard to other tenants…" They answered Jesus' question themselves. I think they'd say it a little quieter if they knew where He was going with it.

The answer is False. In verse 41 the listeners say the other tenants "…will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time." That's the very thing the first tenants wouldn't do. Think of a cookie swap where somebody actually brings cookies, friends.

The answer is that it becomes the cornerstone. Jesus quotes, "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone." (Psalm 118:22; Matthew 21:42). The builders rejected it, and it ends up as the cornerstone. That's quite a turn for one stone, friends.

The answer is True. The Scripture says, "This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes…" (Psalm 118:23; Matthew 21:42). Both halves matter, friends. It's from the Lord, and it's marvelous in our eyes.

The answer is a people who will produce its fruit. Jesus says the kingdom of God "…will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit." The kingdom goes to people who produce fruit. Same word the whole parable has been using, friends.

The answer is that Jesus is speaking about them. Verse 45 says the chief priests and Pharisees "…knew that Jesus was speaking about them." They heard the parables and figured it out. When a story lands that close, nobody has to explain it, friends.

The two words are crowds and prophet. Verse 46 says the chief priests and Pharisees wanted to arrest Him but were afraid of the crowds. So a want and a fear sit in the same verse, friends. The same verse says the people regarded Him as a prophet, and that's why they held back.
